research_caveat: IMPORTANT: the sandbox network egress proxy blocked all direct fetches of metabase.com this session (WebFetch returned EGRESS_BLOCKED; curl CONNECT got 403), so no Metabase page could be fetched directly. Every value below is sourced from Metabase's own pages as surfaced verbatim in domain-restricted web-search snippets (allowed_domains limited to metabase.com). Per researcher hard rules, confidence is therefore capped at 'low' even where the underlying Metabase page is unambiguous. The verifier pass should re-fetch each source_url from an unrestricted network before values are promoted. SCOPE CAVEAT: Metabase does not appear in config/scope.yaml (the 17-vendor list attested 2026-07-31), so the blanket 'soc2_on_file_in_vanta: true' attestation does NOT cover it — check Vanta for a Metabase SOC 2 report before answering 1.4.2. DEPLOYMENT CAVEAT: Metabase's own docs state that for SELF-HOSTED instances Metabase is not a data processor under GDPR (metabase.com/docs/latest/installation-and-operation/privacy); it is a processor only for Metabase Cloud customers (DPA included in the hosting Terms of Service). Confirm with the human that Tavus uses Metabase Cloud — if Tavus self-hosts open-source Metabase, this vendor may not belong on the sub-processor form at all.

3.1.1.locator: Security page, encryption section: 'Data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher'
3.1.1.notes: Snippet-sourced (direct fetch blocked). Documented verbatim as 'TLS 1.2 or higher' — TLS 1.2 is the documented minimum/floor, so the dropdown value 'TLS 1.2' is the supportable choice; TLS 1.3 may be negotiated but is not asserted as the enforced standard. An empirical TLS handshake against metabase.com was impossible (proxy blocks CONNECT). | Corroborated/detailed by Metabase SOC 2 Type 2 (Aug 2024 - Aug 2025, Sensiba), p.11: "During transport (exporting and importing, and backup) we encrypt using SSL & TLS. Connections from the Metabase app server to the database are encrypted using SSL & TLS."

3.1.2.locator: Security page, encryption section: 'sensitive data, like connection strings and settings, is encrypted at row-level with AES256 + SHA512'; 'AWS also encrypts the disks where data is written'
3.1.2.notes: Snippet-sourced (direct fetch blocked). Scope caveat: the documented AES-256 (AES256 + SHA512, row-level) applies specifically to sensitive data such as connection strings and settings; other at-rest data relies on AWS disk-level encryption whose algorithm Metabase's page does not itself specify (do not infer AWS's AES-256 default per the no-inference rule). Mitigating architecture: Metabase keeps customer business data on the customer's own databases and, unless results caching is enabled, does not store query results on its side. Confirm full-scope at-rest algorithm with the vendor. | Corroborated/detailed by Metabase SOC 2 Type 2 (Aug 2024 - Aug 2025, Sensiba), p.11: "The connection details to customer's DW is encrypted at row level with AES-256 CBC and we use SecretsManager to handle keys and associated metadata."

3.1.3.notes: ASSUMED BASELINE per tim@tavus.io convention: encryption confirmed without a named standard; modern enterprise baseline (TLS 1.2+ / AES-256) assumed. Prior evidence retained. | Metabase SOC 2 Type 2 (Aug 2024 - Aug 2025, Sensiba), p.13: "All S3 buckets are encrypted with SSE-KMS and the Metabase encryption key which we create for every customer is saved in AWS Secrets Manager, with access restricted to key personnel"

3.1.4.locator: Security page: 'Key management is in place for encryption keys for production services'
3.1.4.notes: Snippet-sourced (direct fetch blocked). Metabase states it manages encryption keys for its production (cloud) services; no customer-managed key (CMEK/BYOK) offering for Metabase Cloud was found on any retrieved page, so the playbook's managed-cloud default applies. Whether keys are customer-specific is not documented — the value assumes the standard shared-key managed-cloud model; confirm with the vendor and with the human that Tavus's Metabase arrangement involves no customer-supplied keys. (Self-hosted Metabase uses a customer-set MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY per docs/latest/databases/encrypting-details-at-rest — if Tavus self-hosts, the answer flips to 'Key generated by your company' and Metabase is likely not a processor at all; see research_caveat.) | Corroborated/detailed by Metabase SOC 2 Type 2 (Aug 2024 - Aug 2025, Sensiba), p.13: "the Metabase encryption key which we create for every customer is saved in AWS Secrets Manager, with access restricted to key personnel via AWS IAM permissions."

3.1.8.value:
Data-minimization architecture: customer business data stays on the customer's own databases; unless results caching is enabled, no data returned by the customer's database is stored on Metabase's side
Single-tenant isolation: each Metabase Cloud customer runs in its own container (no shared clusters); dedicated single-tenant cloud deployment available on request
Identifiable data in collected usage/telemetry data is hashed
All system calls are logged, monitored and audited, with alerting on calls that indicate a potential intrusion or exfiltration attempt
Independent application-level and infrastructure-level penetration tests several times a year, with findings prioritized and remediated
Daily backups and replication of core databases across zones; backup and restore capability tested annually for disaster recovery
Sub-processor oversight: control reviews of sub-processing vendors before use and at least annually; sub-processors bound to confidentiality commitments; customers notified of new sub-processors via the published list (metabase.com/hosting/subprocessors) with a 10-day objection window
DPA commitment to delete or return all Customer Personal Data at expiry/termination of the agreement (backup/archival copies deleted per retention schedule)
3.1.8.locator: Assembled one-per-line from: metabase.com/security (data minimization, hashing, per-customer containers, system-call logging/monitoring/alerting, penetration tests, daily backups/replication/annual restore tests, key management), metabase.com/cloud (single-tenant option, SOC 2 Type II), metabase.com/license/hosting/original (DPA: sub-processor reviews, confidentiality, deletion/return at termination, 10-day objection window), metabase.com/hosting/subprocessors (published sub-processor list)

open_questions_for_vendor: Please confirm the full legal name, legal form and state of incorporation of the contracting entity for the Metabase Cloud service (Metabase, Inc. — incorporated where?), and confirm the registered address (your public terms list 9740 Campo Rd. Suite 1029, Spring Valley, CA 91977).
Has Metabase designated a representative in the EU under Article 27 GDPR? If yes, please provide the representative's name and full address.

Does Metabase have a formally appointed Data Protection Officer? If yes, please provide name, telephone number and/or email; if not, please confirm legal@metabase.com as the contact entitled to respond to data-protection requests.
Please provide your current SOC 2 Type II report (and confirm whether you also hold a SOC 1 report or any ISO/IEC 27001, 27018, 27701, 22301 or 9001 certification).

Beyond the row-level AES-256 encryption of sensitive data (connection strings, settings), what encryption-at-rest standard protects the Metabase Cloud application database contents (user accounts, queries, dashboards, cached results) — and is it AES-256 at the disk/volume level?
Are backups of customer data encrypted, and with which algorithm?
Who generates and manages the encryption keys for Metabase Cloud — Metabase/AWS with shared (non-customer-specific) keys, or customer-specific keys? Is any CMEK/BYOK option available?

Can Metabase anonymize and/or pseudonymize customer personal data upon the customer's documented instruction (Art. 28(3)(e) GDPR support), as distinct from the hashing applied to your own usage telemetry?
What is the minimum TLS version enforced (you document 'TLS 1.2 or higher') and do you support/enforce TLS 1.3 on all customer-facing endpoints?
Please confirm that the EU (Frankfurt) hosting region covers all processing and storage of customer personal data for an EU-hosted instance, including backups, caching, and support access.
